title: Cache-Aside

validation.research: Five primary references: Microsoft catalogs Cache-Aside and application-owned loading/source-first invalidation; AWS identifies the lazy-loading alias, hit/miss steps and write-through contrast; Jas Chhabra at AWS describes cold/shared/local caches, failure amplification, coalescing and expiration; Python documents monotonic elapsed time and bounded memoization. Lazy Loading (Cache) is disambiguated from deferred object construction. No claim that Cache-Aside alone guarantees consistency, that write-through is inherently atomic, or that TTL establishes source age. Original catalog example, runnable program, controlled race analysis and native figures.

checks: TTL from installation not source age

example_limits: Original catalog price example with immutable integer cents, authoritative in-memory source, two-entry LRU application-owned cache, fixed ten-second TTL from successful fill and injectable monotonic clock. Configuration is trusted positive finite TTL and positive integer capacity. One thread/process, no network/database deployment. Exact outputs: 1200 1200 1; 1300 2; 1300 2; 1400 3; missing not cached True. Source first then invalidation, hit does not renew TTL, equality at expiry misses, missing raises without fill and zero is a valid value. Expired entries removed lazily; capacity bounded. The separate original interleaving shows reader 1200, writer commit 1300, delete, then old fill 1200. The same article implementation is tested under a controlled reentrant load callback to reproduce that race, without claiming concurrency safety. No synchronization, request coalescing, authorization implementation, negative caching, distributed invalidation, stale-source detection, production cache backend, uncertain-write recovery or strict consistency guarantee. Existing Result Caching remains a separate Data Engineering article about valid computed-result reuse; this article specifies application-managed access paths.
